content:
sre-bot: alert: apiserver error-rate spike in eu-west1 (5xxs) :rotating_light:
amelia: seeing ~70% 5xxs on apiserver frontend for last 6m, controller-manager churning too :eyes:
raj: noticed CTL mgr restarts every ~30s, logs show leader-election timeout repeatedly
ben: etctd metrics look fine but wal_sync latency has short spikes (disk iops)
claire: GPU provisioner is backing off in the same region, several attach failures reported -> possible cascade to controlplane queues
amelia: can someone grep controller-manager logs for "failed to acquire leader lease"?
max: running: kubectl -n kube-system logs deploy/controller-manager | grep "failed to acquire leader lease" || true
max: results: a few hundred entries from 2025-11-07T02:14 - suggests leader ping lost when apiserver returns 503s
ben: tail of etcd: "wal fsync took 42ms" and occasional "i/o timeout" around same window
natalie: netstat on apiserver nodes shows high TIME_WAIT and conntrack near limit :warning:
raj: conntrack counts at 94% on nat gateways for eu-west1, probably hitting ephemeral port exhaustion
amelia: that would explain sudden proxy 502/503s and controller-manager election flaps
ben: pulling kube-proxy / lb metrics: apiserver qps steady but request lat distribution has heavy tail from retransmits
claire: GPU attach backlog means autoscaler keeps re-trying pods -> surging watch events to apiserver -> watch fanout blowup
natalie: suggested mitigation: reduce watch traffic by enabling leader-lease-stagger for provisioner and throttle retries on attach
max: temporarily bumped conntrack.max to 262144 on nat nodes, and added iptables rule to drop overly fast retries from provisioner pods
amelia: deployed a canary with attach retry backoff 10s->60s, will reduce watch churn if it holds
raj: restarted controller-manager on two replicas with graceful 60s drain to let lease settle :thumbsup:
ben: still seeing short wal fsync spikes, planning to offload etcd IO to faster NVMe pool in eu-west1; may need maintenance window
claire: what's cost impact of switching to NVMe for etcd? finance wants estimate before we flip
natalie: rough calc: NVMe + iops SLA ~ $2k/month extra for the cluster; compare to cost of losing 1-2% request success—arguably less
amelia: ok prioritize short-term throttles + conntrack bump + retry backoff. If still unstable after 1h, schedule IO migration
max: created a quick dashboard: alerts on conntrack>85%, apiserver_5xx_rate>0.05, etcd_wal_fsync_ms>20ms
raj: added temporary routing fallback so non-critical batch GPU workloads target us-east instead of eu-west to reduce attach pressure
claire: please record rollout steps and rollback plan in the incident doc
amelia: notes: 1) throttle provisioner retries 2) bump conntrack on nat 3) reduce watch fanout via leader-stagger 4) monitor dashboard 5) prepare NVMe migration
ben: I'll open a ticket for NVMe migration and include perf benchmarks, ETA today EOD
natalie: after we stabilize, we should consider reserved GPU capacity window to avoid autoscaler storming during spikes
amelia: heading to runbook update now, ping here when metrics look green :coffee:
sre-bot: incident note appended: runbook-ref: controlplane-watch-throttle-v1
raj: LGTM, marking ops in-progress :white_check_mark:
